title: Idempotency, ETags, and cache-control headers
hook: Networks retry failed requests — without idempotency keys, a duplicated POST can charge a customer twice. ETags and Cache-Control tell browsers and CDNs when they can reuse a response instead of hitting your origin on every request.

blocks.text: An idempotent operation produces the same server-side effect when executed multiple times with the same inputs. PUT and DELETE are idempotent by HTTP definition; POST is not — so payment and order APIs accept an Idempotency-Key header (or custom header) and return the original response on replay. ETags are opaque version tokens for a resource representation — clients send If-None-Match on GET for conditional requests (304 Not Modified). Cache-Control directs browsers and reverse proxies how long a response may be stored.

entries.plainDefinition: A client-generated unique token sent with POST so retries do not duplicate side effects.
An opaque validator for a resource version — often a hash or row version.
Directives like max-age, no-store, private, public that control caching behavior.
Server tells the client the cached copy is still valid — no body is sent.
entries.example: GET with If-None-Match returns 304 when ETag matches

blocks.text: Mobile clients on flaky networks retry POSTs. Load balancers replay requests on timeout. Without idempotency, you double-charge, double-ship, or create duplicate orders. Without Cache-Control, every catalog GET hits your database. Without ETags, clients download unchanged 5 MB JSON blobs. These headers are how senior APIs stay correct under retries and cheap under read load.

blocks.title: Payment API rule
blocks.body: Stripe-style idempotency: same key + same body → replay stored response; same key + different body → 409 Conflict. Store keys in Redis or SQL with TTL (24–72 hours) and the serialized response.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Client generates a UUID key
items.body: One key per logical operation — reuse on retry, never across different charges.

items.title: Server checks key store
items.body: If key exists with same payload hash, return cached 201 response. If key exists with different payload, return 409.

items.title: Process payment once
items.body: Call processor, persist result, store key → response mapping with TTL.

items.title: Client retries on timeout
items.body: Same key hits cache — no second charge.

diagram.title: Idempotency key lookup
diagram.source:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant A as API
  participant R as Redis
  participant P as Payment gateway
  C->>A: POST /charges Idempotency-Key: abc
  A->>R: GET idempotency:abc
  R-->>A: miss
  A->>P: Charge
  P-->>A: success
  A->>R: SET idempotency:abc response TTL 24h
  A-->>C: 201 Created
  C->>A: POST /charges Idempotency-Key: abc retry
  A->>R: GET idempotency:abc
  R-->>A: cached response
  A-->>C: 201 replayed

snippet.label: Idempotency middleware for payments
snippet.explanation: Intercept POST, check Redis for key, replay response on hit. On miss, capture 201 body and store with TTL. Production also hashes request body and returns 409 on key+body mismatch.

snippet.label: ETag conditional GET
snippet.explanation: RowVersion as ETag — client sends If-None-Match on refresh. 304 saves bandwidth. private max-age allows browser cache but not shared CDN for user-specific data.

snippet.label: ASP.NET Core output caching
snippet.explanation: Output caching stores full responses in memory — distinct from HTTP Cache-Control sent to clients. VaryByQuery prevents wrong cache hits. Express equivalent: apicache or CDN cache rules.

snippet.label: Payment service — 409 on key/body mismatch
snippet.explanation: Same key with different amount → 409 Conflict, not silent wrong charge. TTL 48h covers weekend retry windows. Store request hash, not just key presence.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Idempotency keys without TTL — Redis fills forever. Caching personalized responses with public max-age — users see each other's data. ETag from DateTime.UtcNow — changes every second, cache never hits. Storing only 200 responses for idempotency but client retries after 201 — inconsistent replay.

blocks.text: Senior depth for payment APIs: idempotency scope is per merchant + key (not global UUID collision across tenants). Use at-least-once message delivery (SQS, RabbitMQ) with consumer idempotency — same key store as HTTP. Distributed lock is NOT a substitute for idempotency keys — lock expires, retry still double-charges. ETag strong vs weak: strong ETags change when any byte changes; weak (W/"...") for semantically equivalent gzip variants. Cache-Control no-store for PCI responses; s-maxage on public catalog behind Azure Front Door. Prove it: integration test that sends duplicate POST with same key asserts one charge in mock gateway; App Insights tracks 304 rate on GET catalog.

blocks.title: Caching layer tradeoffs
rows: Query string not in cache key
Not shared across pods without Redis backplane
No body hash → wrong replay on payload change

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'POST is idempotent if we check duplicate rows' without a client-supplied key — race conditions still double-charge. Recommending distributed locks alone for payment idempotency. Not knowing 304 responses must not include a body. Caching POST responses at CDN — POST is not cacheable by HTTP semantics.

interviewTakeaways: POST is not idempotent — payment APIs require Idempotency-Key with stored response replay and 409 on body mismatch.
ETags enable conditional GET (304); Cache-Control directs browser and CDN; output cache is server-side another layer.
Store idempotency keys with TTL (24–48h), request hash, and serialized response. Test duplicate POST in integration tests.

60s: Client sends Idempotency-Key on POST. Server checks Redis — hit replays response, body mismatch is 409. ETag on GET — If-None-Match returns 304. Cache-Control public for catalog, private no-store for PII. Locks are not idempotency.
Follow-up: how does idempotency interact with async message consumers processing the same payment event twice?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'we use database unique constraint for idempotency' without client keys gets you rejected — races still occur before commit.
public Cache-Control on authenticated user profile endpoints leaks data through shared caches.
Strong answer: 'Idempotency-Key + body hash in Redis with TTL. 409 on mismatch. ETag from RowVersion. 304 for bandwidth. Output cache for hot GETs. Integration test duplicate POST.'
introducedIn: HTTP/1.1 conditional requests; ASP.NET Core Output Cache in .NET 7

jsTsCorrelations.note: res.set('ETag', hash) and apicache.middleware('5 minutes') mirror ETag and output cache patterns. Stripe's Node SDK sends Idempotency-Key — same header your ASP.NET Core API should accept.

jsTsCorrelations.concept: Cache-Control in fetch and CDN config
jsTsCorrelations.note: fetch cache mode and Next.js revalidate headers interact with Cache-Control from your API. Strong typing for idempotency keys (branded string type) prevents accidental reuse across operations.
